title: Far addressing folds other than the runtime-index fold leave dangling DBG_VALUEs
summary: Three far addressing-mode folds erase or rewrite an access and leave the G_PTR_ADDs that computed its pointer with only debug uses: the absolute-long fold (tryFarAbsoluteAddressing, #320-2), the [dp],Y displacement window in tryFarIndirectIndexedAddressing (#320-4), and the absolute-long indexed fold (tryFarAbsoluteIndexedAddressing, far-word patch 5 / downstream 0061). The legalizer erases the dead adds; salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue cannot express a G_PTR_ADD and leaves the DBG_VALUE on the erased register, which DetectDeadLanes marks undef, so -g with -verify-machineinstrs fails ("Generic virtual register use cannot be undef"). The simplest -g far field access (base + 1) fails at O0 and O2 on the reviewed split and on the downstream release toolchain. Emitted code is unaffected. This is the mechanism of mos-far-index-fold-dangling-dbg (B4) at the fold sites its repair did not cover.

Downstream 0002/0061 are not repaired (vendor/ and 0002 were out of scope for the split work); this closure covers the #320/#321 split series, which is the code being prepared for upstream. A downstream toolchain built from 0002 still fails the baseline input.

prior_work.source_assessment: The reviewed split (#320-2, #320-4, far-word patch 5) and downstream 0002/0061 drop dead-address debug locations only in tryFarRuntimeIndexFold (the B4 repair). The absolute-long, displacement-window and absolute-indexed folds erase or rewrite the access without touching the debug users of the adds that become dead.

prior_work.decision: mos-far-index-fold-dangling-dbg is correctly closed for its own site: its same-input regression passes and its causal change covers only tryFarRuntimeIndexFold. These inputs pass on #320-3 and fail through different fold functions whose code the B4 repair never touched, so they are a distinct defect instance with their own baseline rather than a reopening of B4.

resolution.change: #320 split series: dropDeadFarAddressDebugUses in MOSLegalizerInfo.cpp, called by every far fold that erases or rewrites an access (#320-2 tryFarAbsoluteAddressing, 97a8af8303cc; #320-4 both paths of tryFarIndirectIndexedAddressing, 36d569637f6a; far-word patch 5 tryFarAbsoluteIndexedAddressing, d11ada6289b3). Since the third round it salvages a dead address that is a live base plus constant offsets to base + DW_OP_plus_uconst and sets the rest to $noreg. Round four (2026-10-01) rebuilt these commits without #584; the same changes are now #320-2 df2318f4252a, #320-4 a0e244102ff9 and far-word patch 5 ae450c905cf5.
resolution.causal_explanation: The folds left the G_PTR_ADDs that computed the old pointer with only debug uses; the legalizer erased them and salvageDebugInfo cannot express a G_PTR_ADD, so the DBG_VALUE named an erased register that DetectDeadLanes marks undef and the verifier rejects. The helper rewrites every DBG_VALUE of the dead tree before the adds are erased, so no DBG_VALUE refers to an erased register.
resolution.trigger_check: The unchanged field.ll runs through the repaired #320-4 llc with the baseline's configuration (+mos-a16, -O2, -verify-machineinstrs) and exits 0; the same holds at O0, for store1.ll, gfield.ll (absolute-long site, #320-2) and gidx.ll (absolute-indexed site, far-word top). The reviewed split (c-320-04) fails all of them with the baseline signature, and the series parent of each repair fails its far-fold-debug.ll section.
